name: National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited
summary: A government company that builds highways in the hardest places — the Northeast, the Himalaya, and along India's borders.
ownership: Government of India — Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
about: NHIDCL was set up in 2014 to take on the roads nobody else wanted to build: mountain highways in Arunachal Pradesh and Ladakh, roads through Northeast states with heavy rainfall and landslides, and links to the borders with China, Myanmar and Nepal. Work there is slower and costlier than in the plains — a kilometre of hill road can cost several times a kilometre on flat ground, and the building season is short. It also builds some of India's longest road tunnels, which are the only reliable way through terrain that slides every monsoon.
facts: Works mostly in the Northeast, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
Builds many of India's long road tunnels, which keep mountain highways open in winter.
Also builds road links to the borders with China, Myanmar, Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
